title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: What is the sum of the roots of \(z^{12} = 64\) that have a positive real part?

solutions.text:
The roots of \(z^{12} = 64\) lie on the circle of radius \(64^{\frac{1}{12}} = \sqrt{2},\) at angles that are multiples of \(30^\circ.\) Those with positive real part are at angles \(0, \pm 30^\circ, \pm 60^\circ.\) Their imaginary parts cancel, so the sum is \[ \begin{aligned} &\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{2}\cos 30^\circ \\ &\quad {}+ 2\sqrt{2}\cos 60^\circ \\ &\quad {}= \sqrt{2}\bigl(1 + \sqrt{3} + 1\bigr) \\ &\quad {}= 2\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The twelve roots lie on a circle of radius \(\sqrt{2},\) spaced \(30^\circ\) apart
